elements.element: Customer is not subject to any exclusivity obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 prohibits the Company from participating in similar Internet projects involving Deerskin Products and grants HDI an exclusive right to use the Deerskin brand for the specified website.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not require the Company to purchase products or services solely from HDI or otherwise appoint HDI as its sole supplier.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The restraint is limited to the specified “Deerskin Products” category; the prior references to substantially similar products, named competitors, and similar companies are absent.

elements.element: Any exclusivity binding Customer is limited to 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 6.1 applies only “during the twelve (12) month period commencing on the Effective Date,” notwithstanding the Agreement's potential renewal.

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable service levels.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Company's exclusivity “shall end automatically upon HDI's failure to meet the service levels ... required by this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer's exclusivity ends automatically upon Vendor's failure to meet applicable delivery dates.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence states that the Company's exclusivity “shall end automatically upon HDI's failure to meet the ... delivery dates required by this Agreement.”

result.reason: The rendered clause does not achieve the preferred no-exclusivity position because it retains a direct nonparticipation covenant binding the Company. It does, however, satisfy every fallback requirement by narrowing the product scope, imposing a 12-month cap, and providing automatic cessation upon either service-level or delivery-date failure. The changes are confined to the exclusivity terms and preserve the remaining commercial provisions. Drafting quality is reduced because “the Company's exclusivity” is imprecise: the Company bears a restraint rather than possessing exclusivity, and the sentence does not expressly state whether HDI's exclusive brand-use right also terminates.
